name: Friends and Gifts
description: There are $$$n$$$ friends who want to give gifts for the New Year to each other. Each friend should give exactly one gift and receive exactly one gift. The friend cannot give the gift to himself. For each friend the value $$$f_i$$$ is known: it is either $$$f_i = 0$$$ if the $$$i$$$-th friend doesn't know whom he wants to give the gift to or $$$1 \le f_i \le n$$$ if the $$$i$$$-th friend wants to give the gift to the friend $$$f_i$$$. You want to fill in the unknown values ($$$f_i = 0$$$) in such a way that each friend gives exactly one gift and receives exactly one gift and there is no friend who gives the gift to himself. It is guaranteed that the initial information isn't contradictory. If there are several answers, you can print any.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of friends. The second line of the input contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$f_1, f_2, \dots, f_n$$$ ($$$0 \le f_i \le n$$$, $$$f_i \ne i$$$, all $$$f_i \ne 0$$$ are distinct), where $$$f_i$$$ is the either $$$f_i = 0$$$ if the $$$i$$$-th friend doesn't know whom he wants to give the gift to or $$$1 \le f_i \le n$$$ if the $$$i$$$-th friend wants to give the gift to the friend $$$f_i$$$. It is also guaranteed that there is at least two values $$$f_i = 0$$$.
output_specification: Print $$$n$$$ integers $$$nf_1, nf_2, \dots, nf_n$$$, where $$$nf_i$$$ should be equal to $$$f_i$$$ if $$$f_i \ne 0$$$ or the number of friend whom the $$$i$$$-th friend wants to give the gift to. All values $$$nf_i$$$ should be distinct, $$$nf_i$$$ cannot be equal to $$$i$$$. Each friend gives exactly one gift and receives exactly one gift and there is no friend who gives the gift to himself. If there are several answers, you can print any.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1283C — Friends and Gifts [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
